integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] vstyleh3. One continuous 10-second shot in a spacious daylight workshop. A young adult man with short dark hair, a plain blue long-sleeved shirt, brown trousers and dark ankle boots stands next to a waist-high wooden workbench. His entire body is visible from head to boots throughout the shot. The camera is fixed at a three-quarter front angle, far enough away to include his feet, the workbench, and the floor in front of him. A medium rectangular wooden crate with two open side handles rests near the edge of the workbench. The crate has four straight sides, a flat bottom and visible wooden slats. No other person is present. The wall behind the man has shelves with stationary hand tools; soft light enters through a large window on the left. The floor is level, with ample space around the man. The bench is sturdy and does not move.

During the first two seconds, he leans slightly forward at his hips and reaches towards the crate with both arms. His left hand enters the left side handle and his right hand enters the right side handle. Each hand stays on its own handle for the carrying action. He bends his elbows and lifts the crate clear of the bench, keeping it level in front of his abdomen. His shoulders rotate naturally with the lift, while his torso remains continuous and his head turns towards the open floor on his right. His fingers wrap around the wood rather than passing through it. The crate remains one solid rectangular object with the same dimensions.

From approximately the third to the sixth second, he takes three clear, measured steps to his right and slightly towards the camera, carrying the crate with both hands at waist height. Each step shows a heel placement, a transfer of weight and the trailing foot leaving the floor. His knees bend as he walks, the trousers fold at the joints, and his boots remain attached to his feet. His elbows stay slightly bent. The crate moves with his hands and body rather than drifting independently. The weight of the crate produces a modest forward inclination of his torso, without an exaggerated stumble. Both arms, both legs and the space between them stay visible. He looks towards the location where he intends to place the crate.

From the sixth to the eighth second, he stops walking, places his feet approximately shoulder-width apart, bends both knees and lowers his hips into a controlled squat. He lowers the crate onto the floor in front of him, still holding the same two handles. The bottom of the crate makes contact with the floor before he releases it. The crate does not change shape or penetrate the ground. He opens his fingers and withdraws his hands from the handles. His hands are empty after the release. He then straightens both knees and rises to standing during the final two seconds, allowing his arms to hang naturally at his sides. The crate stays where he placed it. The shot ends with the man standing beside the crate and looking down at it. The camera never cuts, pans or zooms; the man's boots remain in frame. The scene has natural workshop lighting and distinct surfaces on the wood, clothing and skin. The action has ordinary weight, balance and clear contact between hands and crate.

overall_soundscape: A quiet workshop room tone is audible throughout. Fabric rustles with the reach and squat. The wooden crate makes a short soft scrape as it leaves the bench, then there are three separate boot steps across the solid floor. A low wooden thump occurs when the crate touches the floor, followed by faint hand movement at the handles and a last clothing rustle as the man rises. No dialogue.

non_diegetic_music: None.
purpose: new motion scene, not a training caption
